source.title: Adaptive Momentum and Nonlinear Damping for Neural Network Training
source.authors: Aikaterini Karoni; Rajit Rajpal; B. Leimkuhler; Gabriel Stoltz

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some equations and flattened figures/tables show extraction artifacts, but the reported benchmark results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Compares Adam and momentum SGD on held-out loss across several benchmarks after a fixed-budget hyperparameter search. This bears on V4, but does not reproduce the cited optimizer studies’ benchmark recipes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports comparisons for its proposed optimizers too, but those are not rows unless they measure the claim’s Adam-versus-SGD comparison. ResNet-18 is described as having comparable performance across optimizers; its figure does not provide recoverable numerical values. The optimizer search budget and ranges are setup details, not result rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own Adam-versus-momentum-SGD held-out losses on transformer vision and language tasks and ResNet-18. These bear on V4 in new settings. Its 80-trial searches tune momentum and Adam's beta coefficients as well as learning rates, so they do not directly test V4's learning-rate-and-schedule-only premise.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct: the proposed nonlinear-damping methods achieve performance competitive with Adam and reduce the Adam–mSGD gap on the tested transformer tasks, while tuned ResNet-18 optimizers perform comparably. The authors also establish convergence guarantees under their stated theoretical assumptions. CADAM provides no consistent advantage over Adam.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses its own transformer and vision benchmarks, a fixed budget of 80 Optuna Bayesian-search trials per experiment, and omits learning-rate scheduling, weight decay, and gradient accumulation. It does not reproduce the cited optimizer comparison recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The observed Adam–mSGD gap differs across tasks: it is described as substantial on the DistilBERT SST-2 and QNLI tasks, with a notably smaller test-loss discrepancy on QNLI; ResNet-18 optimizers are described as comparable. Optimizer hyperparameters were tuned with 80 trials per experiment.
record.problems: The study searches at most 80 hyperparameter configurations per experiment. GPT2-S results use a single random seed due to computational constraints. ResNet-18 comparisons are described as comparable, but the supplied figure does not yield recoverable numerical values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional Adam-versus-mSGD result rows were recoverable for ResNet-18: Appendix D states that all optimizers were comparable after tuning, but reports the comparison in a figure without recoverable numeric values. Training-loss comparisons are described in text or figures but are not tabulated as separate numerical results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width changes beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.

The learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning regime; a controlled comparison showing that broader tuning causes a reversal; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD; the specifically word-level language-model exception; and worse held-out performance despite equal or better adaptive-optimizer training performance.
Batch-size interventions under fixed epoch budgets and recipes that recover large-batch performance.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and removal of dropout with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All tabulated Adam–mSGD values match the supplied text. Row states describe direction relative to V4's primary adaptive-optimizer disadvantage, whereas verdicts account for V4's tuning qualifications. Reciprocal row pairs should not be counted twice. ResNet-18 parity and training-loss comparisons are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not missing results under the requested rule. Section 5 explicitly states that code is available on GitHub, correcting the record's code_released field.

versions.untested_parts: Network width beyond the interpolation threshold.
Image and language benchmarks outside those studied; broader optimizer tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, and the word-level language-model exception.
Large-batch versus small-batch training under fixed epoch budgets.

relationships.condition: TinyViT image classification and DistilBERT SST-2/QNLI classification; 80-trial searches tuning optimizer coefficients and learning rates, without scheduling or weight decay.
relationships.reason: R1–R6 favor Adam in every task: 0.613 versus 0.647, 0.299 versus 0.345, and 0.340 versus 0.361. These qualify the reach of the adaptive-method disadvantage beyond limited tuning; they do not challenge its restricted premise or establish that broader tuning caused the reversal.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly performed better on TinyViT and both DistilBERT tasks under broader optimizer tuning, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: GPT2-Nano on Shakespeare and GPT2-XS/GPT2-S on OpenWebText under the study's broader optimizer tuning.
relationships.reason: R7–R12 favor Adam: 1.647 versus 1.784, 3.710 versus 3.797, and 3.3008 versus 3.4047. The disadvantage does not extend to these settings; GPT2-S has one seed, and word-level modeling is not established.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly performed better across the GPT2 workloads under broader tuning, but these comparisons remain unverified and GPT2-S used one seed.
